$comment: One industrial story, told once. Every reference scenario in every language
produces THESE events -- that is the whole point of the battery: the
workflow changes, the event meaning does not.
It is a fixture, not an example. examples/ shows what an event looks like;
this is the thing four implementations are checked against, by
VOLATILE fields are listed below and excluded from the comparison. An
event_id is a fresh UUID and a timestamp is the moment of emission: two
correct implementations differ there and are still the same event. What is
compared is what a consumer acts on.
health_index 0.58 with severity 'high' is deliberate. IAES defines no
mapping between them: severity is what the producer ASSERTS and
health_index is a measurement, and the pair demonstrates that they can
coexist without implying a function. A fixture that used a 'matching' pair
would quietly teach a rule the specification does not have.

volatile.$comment: Excluded from cross-implementation comparison, with the reason.
volatile.event_id: a fresh UUID per event, by definition
volatile.correlation_id: generated by the first event of a chain; the STRUCTURE is checked instead -- every later event carries the same one
volatile.source_event_id: a reference to another event's volatile id; the LINK is checked, not the value
volatile.content_hash: optional, and derived from fields that include the volatile ones

story: A vibration model reads 4.2 mm/s RMS on a motor, concludes the outer race of a bearing is degrading, and asks maintenance to inspect it. A technician does, and closes the loop.

data.title: Inspect drive-end bearing
data.description: Vibration velocity at 4.2 mm/s RMS with an outer-race signature. Inspect the drive-end bearing at the next available window.

events.$comment: An event type IAES does not publish, in a namespace the producer controls. Every implementation must accept it: the catalog is open, an unknown event_type MUST NOT cause an error, and an unsupported one may be logged and skipped. This is the scenario that proves IAES is not a closed catalogue of seven Wertek types.
